translations.answer: The detailed baseline in the original thread splits the following: full 16.70 ms, no contact consumers 10.09 ms, cached contact consumers 13.33 ms; solver.update_contacts 0.053 ms, total of four SensorContact.update 0.181 ms, and observed 28 accesses to sensor.data per step. In the 8192-env synthetic benchmark, repeated reads take 2.09 ms, caching 0.43 ms, and solver.update_contacts 0.052 ms. For similar code, statistics should be taken first for the same step, then cache the contact tensor once for reuse in reward/observation; these numbers are only applicable to this benchmark.
translations.applicability: Applicable to IsaacLab develop + Newton, and tasks with repeated reward/observation term access to sensor.data. Different number of sensors and GPU require re-profile.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author upgraded Newton; engineers compared full, no_contact_consumers, and cached_contact_consumers on the same task, and verified it again in the 8192-env synthetic benchmark.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between time-to-first-iteration and ms/step in steady-state, and avoid using 'scaling slow' description.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Timed solver.update_contacts, SensorContact.update, and reward/observation managers, and counted accesses to sensor.data per step.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Runtime: cache the contact tensor once per simulation step and reuse in multiple reward/observation terms.
translations.details.environments.1: Runtime benchmark: IsaacLab develop; Newton backend; Linux 5.15; NVIDIA L40; Dexsuite 64–512 env and synthetic 512–8192 env.
translations.details.limits.0: Startup results come from a single task in the original author, and no complete benchmark table is provided for the upgrade before.
translations.details.limits.1: Runtime testing is not the original author's startup problem, and caching can't explain the 10-minute read; caching is only for partial total steps.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author reported that initializing a large number of environments significantly speeds up, and the maintainer closed it due to the upgrade.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The 512 env caching goes from 16.70 ms to 13.33 ms; repeated reads for 8192 env are 2.09 ms and caching read 0.43 ms.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does Newton 0.2.0 take nearly 10 minutes to start with 4096 env, and does the upgrade resolve it?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: What is the main cost in training runtime per step: Newton core or repeated consumer-side sensor.data updates?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Startup delay is related to Newton 0.2.0 version, and the author reported it disappears after upgrade.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Runtime benchmark shows repeated consumer-side sensor.data updates and materialization are much higher than isolated Newton contact generation.
translations.details.symptoms.0: With Newton 0.2.0 + 4096 env + specific contact pairs, it takes nearly 10 minutes to reach first training iteration; startup speed is acceptable after launch.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Multiple reward/observation terms repeat reading contact sensor in the same step, and the cost increases with more environments.
translations.source.title: Startup Delay and Step-wise Reading Cost for Contact Sensors in Newton are Two Independent Performance Issues
translations.title: How to Determine Whether the Slowness in Step-wise Contact Reading is Due to Repeated Sensor Data Consumption Rather than the Newton Core in IsaacLab/Newton?
